title: Trapping Rain Water
description: Given n non-negative integers representing an elevation map where the width of each bar is 1, compute how much water it can trap after raining.
constraints: Water at boundaries (first and last bar) spills over.

examples.explanation: The elevation map [0,1,0,2,1,0,1,3,2,1,2,1] can trap 6 units of rain water.
Traps 9 units of rain water.

followups: Can you optimize your solution from O(n) space (prefix/suffix arrays) to O(1) auxiliary space using two pointers?
Can this be solved using a monotonic stack? What is the conceptual difference between the two approaches?
How would you extend this to a 3D terrain grid (Trapping Rain Water II) using a priority queue?

title: Merge k Sorted Lists
description: You are given an array of k linked-lists lists, each linked-list is sorted in ascending order. Merge all the linked-lists into one sorted linked-list and return it.
constraints: lists[i] is sorted in ascending order.
The sum of lists[i].length will not exceed 10^4.

examples.explanation: The linked-lists are merged into one sorted list.
Empty array of lists returns null.
An array containing an empty list returns null.

followups: Compare the Min-Heap approach O(N log k) vs Divide and Conquer (pairwise merge sort) approach. What are their memory access patterns and cache behaviors?
What if each linked list is too huge to fit into RAM and resides on external disks across different machines (External K-Way Merge)?
How would you parallelize the merge operation across multi-core CPUs?

title: Word Search II
description: Given an m x n board of characters and a list of strings words, return all words on the board. Each word must be constructed from letters of sequentially adjacent cells, where adjacent cells are horizontally or vertically neighboring. The same letter cell may not be used more than once in a word.
constraints: board[i][j] is a lowercase English letter.
words[i] consists of lowercase English letters.
All strings of words are unique.

examples.explanation: Words "eat" and "oath" can be formed on the board.
No valid non-reusing cell path exists for "abcb".

followups: Why is Trie + Backtracking vastly superior to running standard DFS for every individual word in words?
How do you prune words from the Trie after finding them to speed up subsequent searches?
What is the maximum recursion depth and how do we prevent redundant visits?

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
description: Given an m x n integers matrix, return the length of the longest increasing path in matrix. From each cell, you can either move in four directions: left, right, up, or down. You may NOT move diagonally or move outside the boundary (i.e., wrap-around is not allowed).
constraints: Path must be strictly increasing (matrix[next] > matrix[curr]).

examples.explanation: The longest increasing path is [1, 2, 6, 9].
The longest increasing path is [3, 4, 5, 6]. Moving diagonally is not allowed.

followups: Does this matrix have cycles? Why does strict monotonicity guarantee a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)?
Can you formulate this problem using Topological Sort (Kahn's algorithm) with in-degrees?
What is the time complexity with memoization vs without memoization?

title: Edit Distance
description: Given two strings word1 and word2, return the minimum number of operations required to convert word1 to word2. You have the following three operations permitted on a word: Insert a character, Delete a character, Replace a character.
constraints: word1 and word2 consist of lowercase English letters.
Operations have uniform unit cost of 1.

examples.explanation: horse -> rorse (replace 'h' with 'r'), rorse -> rose (remove 'r'), rose -> ros (remove 'e').
intention -> inention -> enention -> exention -> exection -> execution.

followups: Can you reduce the space complexity from O(m * n) to O(min(m, n))?
How would you reconstruct the actual sequence of edit operations (Diff algorithm / git diff)?
What if different operations have different costs (weighted Levenshtein distance)?

title: Sliding Window Maximum
description: You are given an array of integers nums, there is a sliding window of size k which is moving from the very left of the array to the very right. You can only see the k numbers in the window. Each time the sliding window moves right by one position. Return the max sliding window.

examples.explanation: Single element array.

followups: Can you achieve strictly O(n) total runtime using a Monotonic Deque? Why is each element pushed and popped at most once?
Can this be solved using two passes with block partitioning (prefix/suffix blocks)?
What if k is dynamic or the stream has delayed arrivals?
